name: Central African Republic
tagline: Dzanga Bai, and the forest elephants
summary: Dzanga Bai is a forest clearing where a hundred elephants come to drink mineral water in a single afternoon, and Dzanga-Sangha holds western lowland gorillas habituated for tracking — one of the great wildlife experiences on earth, in one of the hardest countries to reach.
when: December to February, and a shorter window in May and June. Check advice: only the southwest is travelled.

entries.caption: Dzanga Bai
entries.description: A mineral clearing in the forest where a hundred elephants gather in an afternoon.
entries.subject: forest elephants gathered at the Dzanga Bai clearing

entries.caption: The Congo Basin Forest
entries.description: The northern edge of the second largest rainforest on earth, and it starts here.
entries.subject: unbroken rainforest canopy in the Dzanga-Sangha reserve

entries.caption: Western Lowland Gorillas
entries.description: Habituated groups tracked on foot, with far fewer visitors than in the east.
entries.subject: a western lowland gorilla in forest undergrowth

entries.caption: Forest, Not Savanna
entries.description: This is bai-watching and forest tracking. Bongo, forest buffalo and sitatunga, all on foot.
entries.subject: a bongo antelope at the edge of a forest clearing

entries.caption: The Fertit Hills and Mont Ngaoui
entries.description: 1,420 metres on the Cameroon border, in country almost nobody visits.
entries.subject: wooded hills rising above savanna in western CAR

entries.caption: Boali
entries.description: Fifty metres of water on the M'Bali river, two hours from Bangui.
entries.subject: the Boali waterfall dropping over a wide ledge

entries.caption: The Sangha and the Ubangi
entries.description: The Sangha runs down to the Congo; the Ubangi is the whole southern border.
entries.subject: the Sangha river running between walls of rainforest

entries.caption: River Sand
entries.description: Landlocked. The sandbanks on the Sangha come out in the dry season and people use them.
entries.subject: a wide sandbank on the Sangha river in the dry season

entries.caption: Dzanga-Sangha
entries.description: Old-growth Congo Basin forest, shared with Cameroon and Congo as a trinational park.
entries.subject: buttressed rainforest giants in Dzanga-Sangha

entries.caption: Tracking on Foot
entries.description: Gorillas in the morning, the bai in the afternoon, and net-hunting with the BaAka between.
entries.subject: trackers moving quietly through dense forest undergrowth

entries.caption: The BaAka
entries.description: Forest hunter-gatherers whose polyphonic singing is on the UNESCO intangible list.
entries.subject: BaAka women singing in polyphony in a forest camp

entries.caption: BaAka and Sangha-Sangha
entries.description: The BaAka in the forest, and the Sangha-Sangha along the river.
entries.subject: a BaAka net-hunting party moving through forest

entries.caption: Cassava, Bushmeat and Palm Wine
entries.description: Cassava as the staple, smoked fish from the river, and palm wine tapped in the forest.
entries.subject: smoked river fish and cassava on a plate

entries.caption: BaAka Polyphony
entries.description: Sung in overlapping parts, with no leader and no fixed melody, and it has been studied by composers for fifty years.
entries.subject: BaAka singers and drummers around a forest camp fire

entries.caption: Nets, Baskets and Bark Cloth
entries.description: Hunting nets woven from forest liana, and bark cloth beaten from tree fibre.
entries.subject: a woven forest hunting net and bark cloth

entries.caption: Bangui's Colonial Quarter
entries.description: A river capital laid out by the French, and much of it still standing.
entries.subject: a colonial-era building on the riverfront at Bangui

entries.caption: Two Sites
entries.description: Dzanga-Sangha for its forest, and Manovo-Gounda St Floris in the north, on the danger list.
entries.subject: open savanna and gallery forest in northern CAR

entries.caption: Bangui
entries.description: On the Ubangi, opposite the Congo, with the Marche Central at the middle of it.
entries.subject: the Ubangi riverfront and market at Bangui

entries.caption: Colonial and Forest Camp
entries.description: French colonial in Bangui, and leaf-and-sapling mongulu shelters in the forest.
entries.subject: a domed leaf mongulu shelter in a BaAka forest camp

entries.caption: The Marche Central
entries.description: Everything from cassava to river fish, and the noise of a city that never stops trading.
entries.subject: crowds and stalls at the Marche Central in Bangui

entries.caption: Not Yet
entries.description: This is expedition travel in a country with a hard recent history, and it is not for families.
entries.subject: a village school in a forest clearing

entries.caption: Forest Walking
entries.description: Everything here is done on foot, quietly, behind a tracker.
entries.subject: a narrow trail through dense Congo Basin forest

entries.caption: One Lodge
entries.description: Sangha Lodge at Dzanga-Sangha, and nothing comparable anywhere else in the country.
entries.subject: a forest lodge deck overlooking the Sangha river

entries.caption: Dzanga-Sangha's Model
entries.description: The reserve employs BaAka trackers and shares gate revenue with the villages around it.
entries.subject: a BaAka tracker leading visitors through the forest

entries.caption: Elephants in a Clearing
entries.description: Dzanga Bai from the platform at four in the afternoon, when the light comes in sideways.
entries.subject: afternoon light across forest elephants at Dzanga Bai

entries.caption: Chimpanzees at Bai Hokou
entries.description: A second habituated group, and the walk in is as good as the sighting.
entries.subject: a chimpanzee resting in a forest tree at Bai Hokou

entries.caption: Why the Central African Republic
entries.description: A hundred forest elephants in one clearing, watched from a platform, by almost no one.
entries.subject: a viewing platform overlooking elephants at a forest bai
